notes.back:
No. `return name[0]` fails: 'name' is possibly 'null'. initialSafe compiles.

Why: With strictNullChecks, string | null must be narrowed before use. ?. stops at null and ?? supplies the fallback, so every path returns a string.

Docs: TypeScript Handbook — Everyday Types — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/everyday-types.html
notes.quote: With strictNullChecks on, when a value is null or undefined, you will need to test for those values before using methods or properties on that value.

notes.back:
No. `first.toFixed(1)` fails: 'first' is possibly 'undefined'. The `safe` lines compile.

Why: With noUncheckedIndexedAccess, scores[0] is number | undefined, because an index may be past the end. Without the flag the same code compiles and would crash on an empty array.

Docs: TSConfig reference — noUncheckedIndexedAccess — https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#noUncheckedIndexedAccess
notes.quote: Turning on noUncheckedIndexedAccess will add undefined to any un-declared field in the type.

notes.back:
No. `annotated.red.toUpperCase()` fails: toUpperCase does not exist on the tuple type. `checked.red.toUpperCase()` compiles.

Why: An annotation replaces the value's type, so annotated.red is just Color. satisfies checks the object against the type but keeps what it inferred: checked.red is a string.

Docs: TypeScript 4.9 release notes — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-9.html
notes.quote: The new satisfies operator lets us validate that the type of an expression matches some type, without changing the resulting type of that expression.
